title: Embodied : The Art of Being Seen
subtitle: A Yoga & Boudoir Photography Experience

teachers.name: Genevieve Morin
bio: Genevieve has been leading retreats internationally for the last 20 years. She is passionate about worldwide travel, full immersion in different cultures, and the importance of broadening our understanding of one another.

As a trilingual yoga teacher, speaking English, French and Spanish, verbal and non-verbal communication are at the core of her interests. Like cooking or creating music, moving the body, dancing and yogic expression are international, borderless forms of communication. The potential of connection to ourselves, to one another, and to a universal energy is boundless.

Even when Genevieve travels on retreat to a place where common language is not spoken, sharing the language of yoga and movement is always possible. Genevieve loves leading a group of people to unique destinations, especially those who may feel timid or shy in a foreign place. To offer an opportunity for people to experience our human oneness is pivotal and life-changing. We are all human beings with similar needs and desires, and despite borders or differences, we all yearn toward meaningful connections. Genevieve is endlessly intrigued by how simple life truly is… and how simple and joyful our journeys can be.
Discover more about Genevieve on her website, Truro Yoga.

teachers.name: Rachel Gray
bio: Rachel Gray is an internationally recognized photographer, who has worked with leading brands such as Tiffany, Netflix, Time Magazine, and more. Based in Malibu, her work is rooted in both a fine-art foundation and a capacity to capture with presence and sensitivity.

Her work centers on connection — the quiet, unguarded moments where people reveal how they inhabit their bodies and relationships. Clients often describe the experience of working with her as grounding and fun, noting her ability to “conjure vulnerability without imposition.”

During this retreat, you will be guided through an intimate portrait experience that results in an image designed to be treasured for a lifetime. Rachel’s version of boudoir photography is rooted in a light hearted, and playful openness. Participants co-create based on their comfort level and the resulting image is a reflection of each person’s inner landscape.

hero_image.alt: A lone figure on the wide empty shoreline at dawn in El Cuyo, Mexico

intro: Through breath and spontaneous, organic movement, we’ll shake loose the noise and come home to ourselves – not as something to fix, but as something to inhabit.
about_body: Boudoir is deeper than traditional portraiture — intimate not because of nudity, but because of the honesty it captures. It’s a style of photography that reveals how you inhabit yourself: the softness that appears when you stop bracing, the connection that shows up when you’re no longer performing, the presence that emerges when you feel fully at ease.

A yoga retreat is the perfect environment for this kind of work. After days of movement, breath, and grounding practices, most people become more open, relaxed, and connected to themselves than they ever are in daily life. That radiance and ease translates directly into the images — it’s why the portraits created here often feel different from anything someone has tried before.

Participants may be photographed solo or with a partner, always at their chosen level of comfort. Nudity is never required; the only optional form included in this retreat is toplessness, and every image is created with clarity, consent, and care. The process is collaborative, light-hearted, and designed to support expression rather than performance.
– Marking a transition — newlyweds, newly single, post-divorce, postpartum, healing
– Exploring visibility and self-expression in a grounded, supported environment
No experience required — just curiosity, comfort, and a willingness to be met exactly where you are.

accommodations.name: Utopia Guesthouse & Yoga Studio : El Cuyo
text: Utopia Guesthouse & Yoga Studio : El Cuyo is the 3rd incarnation of a series of retreat houses that we have created to host retreat groups over the years.
The main living area shares a sitting room and a dining area indoors. There are porches both on the front side of the house and the beach side.
Bedrooms are simple and cozy with neutral tones, natural textures from local sources and some with ocean views.
The house has 8 bedrooms (5 privates with a queen bed each and 3 shared with 2 twin beds).
Bathrooms are shared amongst the house. There are three full bathrooms plus a double sink wash area upstairs and an outdoor shower with doors on the beach.
Our yoga studio has ocean views from the second story terrace of the house. Yoga mats, blankets, straps and blocks are available.

travel_tips.heading: Yucatán Yoga & Spa Beach Retreat
items: Fly into Cancun International airport (CUN). Please note that Cancun is in the state of Quintana Roo and El Cuyo is in the state of Yucatan and a one hour time difference applies year round. Cancun being one hour LATER than El Cuyo. Please make sure to double check the time zones well as you plan your travel.

From Cancun Airport to El Cuyo, travel time is approximately 2.5 hours door to door. Our drivers are very safe and reliable and we can arrange transfers from the airport to our beach house if you like. Please send along your full flight details and we will try to pair you with others traveling on a similar schedule to and from the retreat. Pricing depends on how many are in the ride.

Taxis are not allowed to wait outside the Cancun International airport at arrivals so a transfer needs to be arranged for a private car service pick up in advance or there is a local bus that takes you to El Cuyo.

For traveling on your own by bus to and from El Cuyo the easiest option is to combine the bus with a taxi. From CUN airport you could take a bus to Tizimin and from there get a taxi to Utopia in El Cuyo and vice versa on the way back. OR you can take a series of local buses between El Cuyo and Tizimin if you want to avoid the $50usd taxi ride. To consult the bus schedule ADO is the most reliable.

There are no ATMS in El Cuyo and everything is better paid in cash as most places do not accept credit cards. Please plan to take out cash in Mexican pesos at the airport ATM upon arrival, pre-order currency from your bank back home and bring it with you or exchange your currency at the airport for Mexican pesos. Some places accept credit cards but it’s always a better idea to have cash just in case. That said there is not a lot of shopping in El Cuyo as it is a quiet town with beach and chill. Cash tips for staff are appreciated

Wifi is not the most reliable and does come in and out at times along with the electricity though it is getting better. If it does go out it usually comes back fairly quickly and offers a nice chance to sit back and relax and watch the stars. If you need super reliable internet please let us know to discuss this further. The idea is to unplug and be offline as much as possible.

There are no specialized stores and although there are a few pharmacies in the town if a specific drug is required, you would have to travel by car to the city of Tizimín about an hour and a half away so please plan on bringing everything you might think you will need with you from home.

faqs.question: Do you accept bitcoin?
answer: In addition to credit card payments we also accept wire transfers, Zelle and Bitcoin. Please inquire for more details.

faqs.question: What is the cancellation policy?
answer: All payments are 100% non refundable and non-transferable. We recommend that you buy trip cancellation insurance immediately upon making your initial deposit to cover any travel hiccups or complications that may arise between now and the time of your retreat. No exceptions are possible so please cover your trip by connecting with an insurance company that offers the right policy for you.

faqs.question: What happens if my travel plans change?
answer: There are no refunds as per our cancellation policies. We highly recommend that all of our guests secure a quality travel insurance that will cover them for any event which may cause a change of travel plans, including personal health issues or personal situations in general which may affect travel plans.

faqs.question: Are flight delays or cancellations covered?
answer: Not by us: transportation delays, cancellations or changes due to strikes, labor disputes, or lockouts from airlines, boats, ferries or any type of transportation are among the events we recommend covering with travel insurance.

faqs.question: Where can I find the full terms & conditions?
answer: The full terms and conditions are published at https://yogaadventuresworldwide.com/termsandconditions/ . By submitting payments toward your retreat you accept them.

booking.balance_note: The balance of your retreat (minus your $750usd initial deposit) is due 90 days prior to arrival. All details with instructions for settling up will be emailed to you three months prior to the retreat.
booking.roommate_note: Roommates should book together. If you would like to share a room and do not have a roommate we will provide one for you if possible. In the case that there is no one to share a room we ask that you take a private room instead.
